svg.text: A mark that is not a colour: one per fighter

Never colour alone. Each fighter has a glyph: a ring (the Protagonist) and a slash (the rival), used on the body, on the aura, on the HUD chip and on the planet strip's marker, so a fighter is told apart with
the colour turned off or confused. Shown in colour, in the three simulated visions and in grey. Working labels, pending Legal review.

Protagonist: a ring. the near shoulder plate: a ring: outer radius 3.9 body units, stroke 1.6, hollow, the gear light colour (#c4ece6) on the dark plate. Aura: solid ring. HUD chip: a circle. Planet strip marker: a circle.

Rival: a slash. across the near upper arm: one diagonal bar from low-left to high-right: 9 body units long, 2.4 wide, the accent light colour (#d9c4f8) on the dark sleeve. Aura: broken ring: dashes 6 px long with 4 px gaps along
the outline (a diagonal stripe mask). HUD chip: a diamond. Planet strip marker: a diamond.

The rule for future fighters: A new fighter gets a glyph from a different family to every existing one (a ring, a slash, then for example a chevron, a bar, a cross of dots), used in the same five places; never a letter or a

number. The glyphs come from the fighters' own shape languages (the Protagonist's circles, the rival's blades), so they also belong to the silhouette. In the aura row the rival's ring is broken into dashes and the Protagonist's is

solid, so the two are told apart in grey at 24 px. The figures here are the approved concept figures with the decal added; the decal sits on the shoulder plate, where a profile and a three-quarter view both show it (it is not on
the chest, which a side view hides).
Data: data/art/colour-vision.json under _non_colour_marks. UI owns the chips and the strip markers; Rendering the decal and the aura pattern (a dash mask on the aura ring).
